heat_surface.narrative: Landsat measured the surface of the ground within 150 m of this address at 3.8°F cooler than the city's land average, over 16 clear summer images from 2023-07-23 to 2026-08-08, each taken at about 11:35 am Eastern Daylight Time; image by image it ran from 2.4 to 4.7°F cooler. In the latest image, on 2026-08-08, the surface here read 93.3°F against a city average of 97.9°F. This is the temperature of roofs, pavement and treetops seen from orbit on clear late mornings, not the air temperature a person feels.

hvi.narrative: The NYC Health Department's Heat Vulnerability Index (2023, from 2016 to 2020 data) scores University Heights (South)-Morris Heights, the neighbourhood around this address, at 5 out of 5, the highest risk group. The index ranks neighbourhoods against each other by a model of heat deaths, from surface temperature, green space, air conditioning, income and the share of Black residents; it is not a measurement of heat at an address, and the department notes that every neighbourhood has residents at risk, whatever its score. For University Heights (South)-Morris Heights the department lists 79.7% of households with air conditioning and 25.9% green space.

heat_visits.narrative: Residents of the Bronx community district 5 made 39 emergency department visits for heat illness in May to September of 2018 to 2022, an age-adjusted rate of 3.9 per 100,000 a year against 6.0 citywide (NYC Health Department, from state hospital records). Visits are counted by where the patient lives, and only when diagnosed as heat illness.

city_landcover.narrative: New York City's 2017 land cover map (6 inch, from LiDAR and aerial imagery) shows that 57.8% of the ground within 500 m of this address is paved or built over and 29.4% is green (23.2% tree canopy); the rest is 12.8% water.

landcover.narrative: Experimental: a satellite land-cover model estimates that 61.8% of the ground within 500 m of this address is paved or built over and 37.4% is green (24.1% tree canopy), on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2026; no change between years is read from it. Limits: it estimates the share of each 10 m satellite pixel that is canopy, grass, paving, roof, water or bare ground, learned from the city's 2017 six-inch map, so detail finer than about 30 m is blurred and a tree over a street counts as canopy; against the city's own 2021 six-inch map, on squares it never trained on, it read a typical district's paved share 1.7 points above the map's (at most 7.8 points off in the 46 districts with enough test ground) and its mean error per land-cover group was 4.8 points at best, more than the 3.0 points of the city's 2017 map read as if it were 2021, so the 2017 map is the more accurate source for its year; two images of one summer differ by under 2.0 points in a district's paved share 19 times in 20, but between 2018 and 2024 the shares of 49 of 59 districts differ by more, so its maps of different years are not compared. Rely on NYC's own land cover maps (2017 and 2021, 6 inch) and building footprints for a survey.
landcover.headline_value: 61.8% paved or built, 37.4% green, 24.1% tree canopy (2026)

heat_obs.narrative: The air at Central Park, the nearest weather station (7.9 km away), was 75°F at 10:51 on 2026-10-02, with a heat index of 75°F. This is the station's reading, not this address's.

heat_station.narrative: At Central Park, the nearest long-record weather station (7.9 km away), the air temperature reached 90°F on 12 days in 2026 through 2026-10-01 and on 14 in 2025; the 1991 to 2020 average is 17 a year. The highest reading of 2026 was 100°F on 2026-07-02, and the station's record is 106°F, set on 1936-07-09 (records from 1869). These are the station's readings, not this address's.
heat_station.headline_value: 12 days at 90°F or above in 2026 (Central Park)

cool_features.narrative: NYC Parks lists spray showers at 9 parks or playgrounds within 800 m of this address (lists updated 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-15); nearest first: Sedgwick Playground (spray shower, 172 m), Plimpton Playground (spray shower, 370 m), Half-Nelson Playground (spray shower, 437 m), Quisqueya Plgd (spray shower, 547 m), Ogden Plimpton Playground (spray shower, 565 m), Wallenberg Plgd (spray shower, 672 m). Spray showers and outdoor pools run in summer only, and the list does not say whether one is working today. Cooling centers are separate: the city opens them only during a heat emergency and lists them then at finder.nyc.gov/coolingcenters (or call 311).

nws_heat_alerts.narrative: No active NWS heat advisory, watch or warning at this point, checked 2026-10-02 15:57 UTC.

nws_heat_forecast.narrative: Over the next 7 days the National Weather Service expects daytime highs of 86°F today, 70°F Saturday, 66°F Sunday, 69°F Monday, 62°F Tuesday, 63°F Wednesday, 69°F Thursday in the 2.5 km grid cell around this place (issued 2026-10-02 10:17 Eastern); the highest apparent temperature it gives, which is the heat index when it is hot, is 85°F on Friday October 2. The Weather Service's New York office issues a Heat Advisory when it expects the heat index to reach 95°F for two days in a row or 100°F at any time, and an Extreme Heat Warning at 105°F for two hours. The Weather Service wrote this for an area; it is not a prediction for a building.
nws_heat_forecast.headline_value: high of 86°F forecast in the next week

npcc4_heat.narrative: NPCC4 (2024) projects 38 to 62 days a year at or above 90°F in New York City by the 2050s and 46 to 85 by the 2080s, as its middle range (25th to 75th percentile), against 17 a year in 1981-2010; the 90th percentile is 69 days by the 2050s and 108 by the 2080s. Days at or above 95°F go from 4 a year to 14 to 32 by the 2050s and 17 to 54 by the 2080s, and heat waves from 2 a year to 5 to 8 and then 6 to 9. The ranges pool 16 climate models and two emissions scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5), and are for the city as a whole, not for a neighbourhood.
